title: Intermediate Grammar (Essential Grammar in Use - Murphy)
lesson_overview: B1 level introduces complex structures for more flexible communication, including conditionals and reported speech.

topics.name: Conditionals
topics.lesson_text: Conditionals describe results of conditions. Zero Conditional: if + present, present (general truths: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils). First Conditional: if + present, will (real future: If it rains, I will stay home). Second Conditional: if + past, would (unreal present/hypothetical: If I won the lottery, I would travel). Third Conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past: If I had studied, I would have passed). Mixed conditionals combine time references. Note: unless = if not. Conditional sentences with 'unless', 'as long as', 'in case'.
examples: If you mix red and white, you get pink.
If I have time, I will call you.
If I were rich, I would buy a boat.
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

topics.name: Passive Voice
topics.lesson_text: Passive voice focuses on the action/recipient rather than the doer. Structure: be + past participle. Form: am/is/are + past participle (present), was/were + past participle (past). By-phrase: The window was broken by the boy. When doer is unknown: The book was published in 2020. Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle. Note: Not all verbs can be passivized (intransitive). Sometimes 'get' used informally: He got fired.
examples: The report has been written by the team.

topics.name: Reported Speech
topics.lesson_text: Reported speech (indirect speech) reports what someone said without quoting directly. Statement changes: pronouns, time/place words shift back (today -> that day, now -> then). Verb tense backshift: present -> past, past -> past perfect. Questions: reported question word + if/whether + statement form. Commands: tell/ask/order + object + to-infinitive. Reporting verbs: say, tell, ask, explain. Note: sometimes no backshift if statement is still true.
examples: She said "I am tired" -> She said she was tired.
He asked "Do you speak English?" -> He asked if I spoke English.
The teacher said "Open your books" -> The teacher told us to open our books.

topics.name: Gerund/Infinitive
topics.lesson_text: Gerund (-ing form) functions as noun. Infinitive (to + base verb) functions as noun, adjective, adverb. Verbs followed by gerund: enjoy, mind, suggest, appreciate, finish, risk. Verbs followed by infinitive: want, need, decide, hope, promise, learn. Verbs followed by gerund or infinitive with meaning change: start, begin, like, love, hate. Adjectives + infinitive: happy to see, glad to help. Nouns + gerund: difficulty in doing, importance of doing. Note: Some verbs take object + infinitive: want somebody to do something.
examples: There is no point in waiting.

cefr_description: Can deal with most situations likely to arise whilst travelling in an area where the language is spoken.
